the_claim: A precondition is not knowledge to acquire and not a parameter to train. It is a DECLARATION the program makes in the one channel nobody reads: the refusal. Six clause forms are read from the program's own sentence, and resolving the largest of them -- a missing enclosing world -- took git from 3 doors in 480 refusals to 438.

measured_doors_same_seeds.note: identical seed, identical script, before and after on the same machine; the only change is the repair pass

WORLD.sentence: fatal: not a git repository (or any of the parent directories): .git
WORLD.mechanism: the program declares the operation that CREATES the world it says is missing; `git init` is among git's own admitted subcommands

UNLOADABLE.mechanism: substitute a file whose CONTENT is the kind named
UNLOADABLE.why_zero: with a plain-text seed the environment has no certificate to substitute; with a real certificate in the seed the same form answered 22 more in the rich-seed run, so this is a seed-content limit and not a reading failure

WITNESS.why_zero: same seed-content limit: nothing in a plain-text trial is a certificate

ENUMERAL.why_nearly_zero: the alternatives are MODES, and each mode has its own further precondition (a recipient, a signer key) that the trial's seed cannot supply; one mode needed nothing more

OFFERED.why_zero: the offered flag names an artifact that must already exist

RANGE.why_zero: re-binding the declared numeric slot to 0 removes the range error and the operation then fails for a different reason (the input is not DER), so the tree does not change

CONFLICT.sentence: You may not specify more than one '-Acdtrux' ... option
CONFLICT.why_zero: tar names the GROUP, not which of this command's flags is in it; removing each member in turn does not clear the conflict

the_honest_sizes_per_clause_form.aggregate_honesty: ONE FORM did the work. 435 of the 436 answers came from the world clause; the other five forms answered 1 of 138. An aggregate number would present a tuned reader as a general one, which is why both figures are reported.

the_rich_seed_run.result: openssl 24 -> 54 doors, 465 of 1036 refusals answered across 9 programs
the_rich_seed_run.why_it_differs: UNLOADABLE and WITNESS can only answer when the environment CONTAINS a file of the kind asked for; a plain-text trial contains none, so the same reader scores 0 there. Both numbers are real and neither is the whole truth without the seed it was measured on.

the_mechanism_in_one_sentence: Read the sentence the program wrote, supply the one thing it named, put a FLAG where the option parser will see it and a VALUE where the operands are, and let the tree say whether it paid.
why_the_placement_matters: `openssl cms -stream in.txt -encrypt` answers 'No operation option specified' because openssl stops reading options at the first operand; the same flag before the operand works. This is the defect round 7 found in the binder, and the first version of this module reintroduced it by appending.
the_oracle_repair: `git init` creates `.git/` and changes no file, so a file-only digest reported world_created: False for a world that had plainly been created. The digest now walks directories. The same blindness exists in tool_census_v1 and is NOT fixed there in this round -- recorded as an open item rather than silently patched.
what_this_does_not_say: It does not say the reader generalises. Measured on 9 programs it had never been touched for (git, openssl, tar, zip, install, find, sed, patch, jq) the non-world forms answered 1 of 138. The world clause is the mechanism that generalises; the other five are read but do not pay on this seed.

It does not validate the world clause on a second program: no second toolchain (npm, cargo, go, terraform) is installed in this sandbox, so `npm init` style worlds are unmeasured. The mechanism reads ONLY the program's own admitted subcommands, so it is not git-specific by construction -- but that is an argument, not a measurement.

It does not resolve the four open questions from round 7. It answers what to save: the reliability of READING a clause form, not the action. A saved action expires with the environment; `world clause -> resolve with the program's own initialiser -> paid` does not.
honest_limits: 435 of 436 answers are one clause form from one program; presenting 61 -> 497 as general would be the reporting this project forbids
the reader's non-world forms are tuned on openssl's phrasing and scored 1/138 on unseen refusals
UNLOADABLE/WITNESS cannot pay without a seed that contains the artifact kind asked for
no second toolchain is installed, so the world clause is measured on git alone
a repair writes only inside a temporary tree; nothing is written to the repository and no temporary tree is left behind (checked)
authority NONE, sandbox only; independent verification OPEN
